root_cause.text: The RSI911x mac80211 driver failed to set `hw->vif_data_size`, so `ieee80211_vif` objects were allocated without the trailing driver निजी storage, yet the driver still wrote its `struct vif_priv` into `vif->drv_priv`, causing an out-of-bounds write and memory corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `hw->vif_data_size = sizeof(struct vif_priv);` in `rsi_mac80211_attach()`, and the CVE description states that without this size the kernel allocates no driver-data space past `struct ieee80211_vif`, while `rsi_mac80211_add_interface()` writes `vif_info->vap_id = vap_idx` through `vif->drv_priv`, corrupting adjacent memory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set the per-VIF private data size so the driver can store its interface-specific state correctly.
intent_record.what: A new assignment was added in rsi_mac80211_attach(): hw->vif_data_size is set to sizeof(struct vif_priv) immediately after hw->extra_tx_headroom is initialized.
intent_record.how: This makes mac80211 allocate per-VIF private storage of the specified size for this driver, enabling the driver to associate private data with each virtual interface during runtime.

grouping_result.intent: Set the per-VIF private data size so the driver can store its interface-specific state correctly.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it sets the per-VIF private data size (`hw->vif_data_size`) so `ieee80211_vif` allocations include the driver’s trailing private storage, preventing the out-of-bounds write to `vif->drv_priv`.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix setup block configures the mac80211 hardware but omits the required hw->vif_data_size assignment. The missing per-VIF private storage size is the root cause that allows later writes to vif->drv_priv to overflow allocated memory.

vuln_statements.explanation: This initialization block is where the driver should also have set hw->vif_data_size for per-VIF private storage. The omission in this setup path caused ieee80211_vif allocations to lack space for drv_priv, leading to the out-of-bounds write described in the root cause.
